blocks.text: Matter is a planner for your Mac that knows how much a day holds. Everything you create lives on your Mac and in your own iCloud — there are no accounts to make, and nothing is uploaded to us.
This guide walks through each part of the app. Use the contents to jump to a topic, or read straight through.
The main pages
**Tasks** — your board of things to do, with a live view of how the day's plan fits your time.
**Calendar** — your days and events, from calendar feeds you subscribe to.
**Notes** — a block-based space for longer thinking, organized into folders.
**Standup** — a free-form daily log for reflection, one entry per day.
Getting started
Open **Tasks** and add a few things you need to do with **New task**.
Set your work hours and focus cap in **Settings ▸ General** so the capacity reading reflects your real day.
Give tasks an estimate so Matter can tell you whether the day actually fits.
Explore the rest — subscribe to a calendar, jot a note, or write today's standup.
Your data stays on your Mac and in your own iCloud. See the **Privacy Policy** for exactly what that means.
The Tasks board is Matter's home. It shows your open work in two columns — **Today** and **Upcoming** — with completed items kept in view for the day you finish them.
Creating and editing
Click **New task** at the top of the Tasks page to create a task.
A task has a title, a day (today unless you pick another), an optional time, an estimate, and any number of tags. Only the title is required.
Click any task row to open the editor. Press **Done** to save, or **Cancel** (Esc) to leave it as it was.
Scheduling a task
Pick a day for the task, and optionally a time. If you set a time, the task is *pinned* there. If you leave the time empty, Matter auto-places it within your day's available time.
Clear a task's time at any point to hand its placement back to auto-scheduling.
Completing, reopening and pushing
Click the circle on a row to mark it **done**. Click the checkmark again, or choose **Reopen** from its menu, to reopen it.
Hover a row and use the **+** menu to push a task to tomorrow, out a few days, or to next week.
If you keep pushing the same task, Matter asks you to confirm — a gentle nudge that it may need rethinking.
Archiving and deleting
Deleting a task asks first, then moves it to the Archive. Open the Archive from the toolbar to reopen finished tasks or restore deleted ones.
Tags on the board
A task appears under each tag it carries. The Today column groups rows by tag, with each group showing the tag's symbol and its total estimated time. Untagged tasks appear under **No tag**.
Tracking time

Drag a task onto the **work bucket** at the bottom of the sidebar to start timing it. Its clock counts down against the estimate, then keeps going past it. It stays there on every page. See **Capacity and scheduling** for how tracked time feeds your day's budget.
Finding a task
Use **Quick find tasks…** in the toolbar to filter by title.
Matter doesn't just list tasks — it tells you whether they fit. It compares the time you've planned against the time you actually have, and says so before the day is overcommitted.
Your day's shape
**Work hours** — the window your day runs in, from **Start of day** to **End of day** (8am to 8pm by default). Only time inside this window counts.
**Focus cap** — the most focused work a day holds (6 hours by default). A day's budget is the smaller of this and the time the day has left.
Set both in **Settings ▸ General**. By default a full day refuses new work; turn that off and it only says so.
The capacity reading

The sidebar shows today's capacity in one line: how much time is free, or how far over you are, with the timer turning orange. Click it for a breakdown of worked, planned and free time, for the whole day and from now on.
The today gate
When you give a task an estimate that won't fit today, the editor says so — **Doesn't fit today** — and offers to move it to the soonest day that has room.
Auto-placement
Tasks without a set time are placed automatically into the earliest open slot that fits their estimate, working around anything you've pinned to a specific time.
Events that count

Calendar feeds can be set to **count toward your load**, and they do by default. When on, their events consume capacity just like tasks. When off, they're shown as context but don't affect your budget. Change this per feed in **Settings ▸ Calendars**.

Templates turn work you do again and again into tasks that arrive on their own. Each template has the days it repeats on, an estimate and tags, and adds a real task on each of those days. Coming ones show faintly on the board.
Creating a template
Open the **Templates** panel from the toolbar.
Click **New template** in the **Weekly** or **Monthly** section.
Fill in the title, then when it repeats (every day, weekdays, any days you pick, or dates in the month), its estimate and tags. Press **Done**.
Applying templates by hand
Each section's **Manually apply** adds the period's tasks now instead of each on its own day: the rest of this week for Weekly, this month for Monthly.
A weekly template shows its week as squares: solid when the day's task is on the board, light when it will come on its own.
A monthly template shows a checkmark once this month's task exists. Applying twice never makes duplicates.
What its tasks inherit
Tasks created from a template start with the template's estimate and tags, and behave like any other task from then on — you can reschedule, retag, or complete them freely.
Tags are how you group your work. A task can carry several tags, and the board organizes around them.
Managing tags
Open the **Tags** panel from the toolbar to add a tag or edit an existing one.
Tags sit under tag types, such as Clients. Each has a name and a symbol. Add, rename, hide, move and drag to reorder them in place.
Applying tags
In a task's editor, click **Add tag** to choose its tags. On the Today column, tasks are grouped under each tag they carry, with the group showing the tag's symbol and its total estimated time.
Events from calendar feeds can be tagged too — the tag is stored in Matter and never written back to the feed.
Matter can bring your external calendars in alongside your tasks by subscribing to iCal (ICS) feeds. Matter only reads a feed — it never edits or writes back to your calendar provider.
Subscribing to a feed
Open **Settings ▸ Calendars**.
Click **Add a feed…**, enter a name and the feed's link (https:// or webcal://), then click **Add**. The feed is fetched right away.
Pick a color for the feed, and decide whether it should **count toward your load**.
A feed's link usually comes from your calendar provider as a “subscribe” or “iCal/ICS” link. Matter needs the feed itself, not a web page.
Managing feeds
Click a feed's eye to pause syncing it without deleting it.
**Refresh all** forces a live re-fetch and shows the last sync time.
Deleting a feed removes all of its events from the board and the Calendar page.
How syncing works

Matter syncs on a periodic timer, when the app becomes active, and whenever you hit Refresh. It keeps a rolling window of roughly a month back and a month ahead, and expands repeating events (including edited single occurrences) so they land on the right days.
The Calendar page
Switch between **Daily** and **Weekly** views. Days and hours form a grid, with events and scheduled tasks drawn as blocks.
Use the **‹ ›** arrows to move between days or weeks; past days fade so the week reads as a record.
Click an event to see its title, time, place and calendar, and to add your own notes and tags.
You can start a work session on an event, just like a task.
Notes is a space for longer thinking — a list of notes on the left, a rich block editor on the right. Notes can be filed into folders or left unfiled.
Organizing notes
Click **New note** to start one; it opens in the editor immediately.
Create folders and drag notes into them to file them. Unfiled notes collect under **Notes**.
The list is searchable by title and by the text inside a note.
Deleting a note removes it for good.
Matter reopens the last note you were reading when you return to the page.
The block editor
Notes (and Standup) share a block-based editor. Every line is a block you can restyle and rearrange:
**Block types:** type **/** for text, headings, bulleted and numbered lists, and checkable to-do items.
**Indent** with Tab and outdent with Shift-Tab to build nested structure.
**Inline formatting:** bold (⌘B), italic (⌘I), underline (⌘U) and strikethrough (⇧⌘X).
**Date chips:** type **@** to pick a date and drop in a date token.
**Keyboard:** arrow keys move between blocks, Return splits a block, and Backspace at the start of a line merges it upward.
Your edits save automatically a moment after you stop typing.
Standup is a daily reflective log — one entry per day — built for a quick check-in with yourself. It uses the same block editor as Notes.
A day's entry
Click **Add today** to create today's entry if it doesn't exist yet.
Each entry is organized around a few fixed prompts, and each prompt has its own editable block area.
Past days are listed newest-first in the sidebar; select one to revisit it.
Matter can remind you 30, 5 and 2 minutes before an event with a time, as macOS notifications, while it is open.
Turn reminders on in **Settings ▸ General**.
If you said no to notifications before, **Turn on** opens System Settings so you can allow them.
Matter is a single window with a handful of pages and a side panel that opens beside them.
Switching pages
The icons at the top of the sidebar move between **Tasks**, **Calendar**, **Notes** and **Standup**.
Open Settings any time with **⌘,**.
The sidebar and toolbar
The **capacity reading** at the foot of the sidebar shows free or over-planned time at a glance.
**New task** creates a task.
The **pin** at the top of the sidebar (⇧⌘N) opens the notebook, a scratchpad that stays with you across pages.
Panels and sheets

The notebook, Templates, Tags, Archive and Week review open in a side panel at the right of the page; the panel button at the end of the toolbar, or ⌃⌘I, closes it or brings back the last one. The task editor and event details open as sheets; press **Esc** to close them.
Settings
Settings has two tabs, **General** and **Calendars**. Links to this guide (**Support**) and the privacy policy are at the foot of **General**, and in the Help menu.

Matter is a local-first app. Your tasks, notes, calendars and settings are stored on your Mac and, if you use iCloud, in your own private iCloud database to keep your Macs in step. None of it is sent to us. Matter has no account system, no analytics, and no advertising or tracking.
What stays on your Mac
Everything you create in Matter — tasks, templates, notes, standup entries, tags, and preferences — is stored on your Mac. We, the developer, never receive this data.
iCloud

When your Mac is signed in to iCloud, Matter keeps a copy of your data in your private iCloud database, so your Macs stay in step. That database belongs to your Apple Account and is governed by Apple's privacy policy. We cannot see or reach it.
Calendar subscriptions

If you subscribe to a calendar feed, Matter periodically fetches it directly from the link you provide. Those requests go to that calendar's server, governed by that provider's own policies. Matter does not route them through us.
Nothing else goes out
Apart from iCloud and the calendar feeds you add, Matter makes no network requests. It contains no third-party code that collects data, and no crash or usage reporting of its own.
Data you export or share
If you copy, export, or share content out of Matter, that action is yours and leaves Matter's control.
Children
Matter is not directed at children and does not knowingly collect information from them.
Changes
If this policy changes, the updated version will appear on this page, with its date.
Contact
Questions about privacy? Write to support@trymatter.app, or reach us through the **Support** page — in the app, Help ▸ Matter Support.
